## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials in this search yet. In generation 0, all 84 trials scored 0 on both training and dev, so the problem is getting the agent to learn at all, not to generalise to new designs. Changes to the default-range recipe, to head design and to model families all failed, and none of them could be ranked against another. Three things were never tried: lr above 2e-3, n_envs above 256 and gae_lambda below 0.9. Smaller networks were also never tried, and neither were standard PPO details like orthogonal initialisation with a near-uniform starting policy (gain 0.01 on the policy outputs) and normalisation layers. This round tests those gaps in a controlled way. P1 keeps the starting network and uses a recipe that gets the most samples and gradient steps: 1 epoch, 1024 envs, lr 3e-3 and lambda 0.8. P2 is the same as P1 plus orthogonal init, so P1 vs P2 isolates the init. P3 is a smaller network with GroupNorm, trained on a different untried recipe. Any nonzero score from these is informative.

### Round 2
After 87 trials, every one has scored 0 on dev and 0 on training. That includes all of round 1: more samples, lr 3e-3, n_envs 1024, gae_lambda 0.8, orthogonal init, a smaller net and GroupNorm. The rules check whether 8,192 training steps give more than 25% exact builds. That cap only makes sense if the described task is easy to learn, so this world probably breaks one of the stated assumptions. Recipe changes have not helped, so I will stop tuning the recipe on its own. There are three likely kinds of mismatch that a local conv net cannot correct: (a) the target or action frame is flipped or transposed relative to the build frame; (b) DONE or the action indices are not where the spec says; (c) the reward is sparse or the horizon long. Each proposal targets one of these, using cheap, learned and general mechanisms. A nonzero training success in any trial would point to which one it is.

### Round 3
After about 90 trials across many worlds and families, every result is 0.000 on both dev and train success. That includes the 6 trials here: large batches with a high lr, orthogonal init, a small normalised net, dihedral input, a global per-action bias, and a long-horizon, high-entropy recipe. Because there is no variance, seed noise cannot be measured and no idea can be ranked. Training success is zero, so the agent is not learning at all; this is not a generalisation gap. The likely cause is something about this world that local conv heads cannot adapt to, or something no network can fix (reward, DONE or mask behaviour). These three trials test axes nobody has tried. The first combines lambda 0.99, clip 0.3, entropy 0.05, gamma 0.9 and 4 large minibatches. The second adds coordinate channels and a dilated, global-broadcast CNN. The third is an MLP-Mixer whose token-mixing layers can learn any fixed position-to-position map, for example a shifted or permuted frame.

### Round 4
After 93 runs that all scored 0 (84 in generation 0, 9 earlier in this search), r3c2 is the first that learned: 0.150 and 0.543 dev success on its two seeds, and 0.27 training success. Its main new parts were constant y/x coordinate channels, dilated residual convs that see the whole grid, and global context added to every cell's features. Two of these do not explain the jump. Global broadcast alone (r2c2) scored 0. The Mixer (r3c3) also saw the whole grid and scored 0. That leaves absolute position, the coordinate channels, as the most likely key: the world probably has a quirk that depends on position. The gap between the two seeds (0.39) is large, so single runs tell us little. With one round left, all three proposals keep r3c2 and make one change each: more samples (fewer PPO epochs), a near-uniform starting policy to make seeds more consistent, and stronger position features that also reach the action head.
